text:
This one stat shows why Amazon shares have a lot more room to run 
MARKETWATCH 7:37 AM ET 1/9/2018 
Critical information for the U.S. trading day 

By the very early looks of it, this year could be shaping up to be another winner for stocks, as many of 2017's hot shots sprint out of the gate. 

Netflix (NFLX) , up 55% in 2017, has gained 10% just a few days into the new year, while Facebook (FB) is nearly 7% higher, after a 61% gain last year. It's tough to fault investors who are gobbling up stocks as fast as they can (http:/ /www.marketwatch.com/story/be-afraid-investors-are-eating-up-stocks-at-the-fastest-pace-in-years-2018-01-08) and dumping those just-in-case-it-all-goes-pear-shaped ( https://www.wsj.com/articles/as-stocks-reach-new-highs-investors-abandon- hedges-1515421800) hedging-strategies. 

Of course, we may all eventually get burned by a meltdown. On that note, check out our chart of the day , which shows how one of the brightest stars in the stock universe -- Apple -- tends to run into big selloffs every few years. 

Our call of the day is not about to spoil anyone's fun, though, when it comes to another one of last year's big performers. It comes from Michael Olson and Sam Kemp, analysts at Piper Jaffray, who say Amazon (AMZN) shares have a lot further to run. That's because, in contrast to common belief, its biggest market still holds lots of room for more sales -- even though Amazon just polished off its best shopping season to date ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/what- americans-bought-on-amazon-this-holiday-season-2017-12-26). 

The analysts recently surveyed 1,000 U.S. internet users and found the biggest chunk of that group earmarked 0% to 10% of their 2017 holiday spending to Amazon. They also estimated that the Amazon grabbed just a 4% share of last year's overall U.S. retail holiday spend. 

"The conclusion is that Amazon, despite its size and continued strong growth, is arguably still in the early innings of its share gain potential, even in the company's most penetrated market," write Olson and Kemp. 

The Piper Jaffray pair upped their price target for Amazon to $1,400 from $1,200 a share, sticking to an overweight rating. 

Amazon disappoints no one when it comes to its ambitions, with talk of a possible Target acquisition (https:// www.forbes.com/sites/chuckjones/2018/01/08/buying-target-increases-amazons-eps-by-5-to-8/), a push into health care ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cardinal-health-fires-back-at-amazon-health-care-threat-you-cant-beat-our-prices-2018- 01-08) and its launch in Australia ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amazon-finally-launches-in-australia-but-its-a- patchy-start-2017-12-05). But it may just be its core strategy that keep those shares moving higher: Americans who would rather shop from the comfort of their phones. 

Plus: Surprise, surprise, Americans are not taking on too much debt ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/surprise- americans-arent-taking-on-too-much-debt-2018-01-09) 

Key market gauges 

Dow futures show that index may be ready to resume a record run. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are also up. Asia had another upbeat day ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-continue-their-early-year-rally-2018-01-08 ), with the Hang Seng index continuing its own string of record closes. European stocks remain at their highest levels since 2015 ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-for-5th-session-in-a-row-stay-at-highest-since-2015-2018-01-09 ). 

The dollar is up a bit, gold is off, and oil prices have turned flat ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices- extend-recent-gains-hint-at-fresh-3-year-highs-2018-01-09). 

Check out Market Snapshot ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-on-track-to-resume-record-run-after-taking-a-breather- 2018-01-09) for more. 

( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/crude-oil-rises-to-1-week-high-on-signs-of-slower-us-drilling-activity-2017-12- 18)Bitcoin has slipped under $15,000 ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ripple-falls-making-ethereum-the-second-biggest- cryptocurrency-once-again-2018-01-09), while ether coins cling to $1,200. Meanwhile, Direxion Asset Management has pulled its request to launch five bitcoin-based ETFs ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/proposal-for-risky-bitcoin-based- etfs-withdrawn-2018-01-08), after regulators raised concerns.

The chart 

As you revel in these market highs, here's some food for thought: Even the losers get lucky sometimes, and even the winners have bad days. 

Heard it all before? OK, but here's a chart sent over by Sean Emory, founder of Avory & Co ( https://www.avory.xyz/ ). (he blogs at The Market Meter ( https://www.themarketmeter.com/ )) that points out how even the mighty take a fall now and then. 

It shows drawdowns -- the drop from a peak to a low -- since 2004 for Apple (AAPL) . 

"This is arguably the most important company of our generation and maybe all time, yet in its third decade of existence, the market still sends it lower by 30% every 2.8 years on average," notes Emory. 

Read:Apple hits back at criticism its devices are addicting kids ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-defends-its- record-amid-criticism-over-iphones-effect-on-kids-2018-01-08). 

The buzz 

North Korea plans to send athletes ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/north-korea-to-send-athletes-to-olympics-in- south-2018-01-09) -- and even cheerleaders -- to next month's Winter Olympics in South Korea. 

GoPro (GPRO) is down a bit in premarket after Monday's roller coaster ride ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gopro- shares-pare-huge-loss-on-report-company-is-exploring-sale-2018-01-08). Still, there might be one more thing the company can do -- kick out CEO Nick Woodman ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/its-time-for-gopro-founder-ceo-nick-woodman-to-go- 2018-01-08).

Alibaba (BABA) is seriously considering a Hong Kong listing, says founder Jack Ma ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ alibaba-will-consider-listing-in-hong-kong-says-jack-ma-2018-01-09). 

SpaceX, led by Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk, has suffered a setback after the failed launch and possible loss of a classified military satellite ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/top-secret-satellite-lost-in-botched-spacex-launch- report-2018-01-08). 

Looking for a reason to get into emerging markets? Larry Tentarelli of Trend Trading Signals (https:// trendtradingsignals.com/blog) says they're getting ready to move higher.
